newsitem.title: USA: Simpson testimony delayed; custody ruling imminent.
newsitem.headline: Simpson testimony delayed; custody ruling imminent.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's second round of testimony at his civil trial was postponed on Friday as he awaited a family court judge's ruling in his bitter fight for custody of his two young children.

The former football star, who had been scheduled to take the witness stand on Friday, was reportedly huddling with his legal advisers to learn whether he would get back the children he had with Nicole Brown Simpson.

A source involved in the case said Simpson, who last month faced three days of harsh interrogation by opposing attorneys, would not take the stand again until sometime after the two- week holiday break.

Simpson's attention on Friday appeared to be focused on his child-custody battle. Louis and Juditha Brown have been caring for their grandchildren, 11-year-old Sydney and 8-year-old Justin, since just after their daughter was killed in June 1994.

Simpson, who was acquitted in October 1995 in the killings of his former wife and her friend Ronald Goldman, is now on trial in civil court facing a wrongful-death lawsuit brought by the victims' families.

Simpson turned over temporary guardianship of the children to their maternal grandparents after his June 17, 1994, arrest. He now wants them back, but the Browns have refused and are seeking legal custody.
At the civil trial, amateur photo analyst Robert Groden returned for a second day of testimony, only to come under bruising cross-examination by plaintiffs' attorney Peter Gelblum.
Groden testified on Wednesday that a 1993 photograph of Simpson apparently wearing the same kind of expensive designer shoes worn by the killer is most likely a fake.
But Gelblum lashed into Groden on Friday, pointing out he had no qualifications or formal training in photo analysis and suggesting he was a conspiracy buff who was testifying for the money.

Groden, a Dallas photo technician who dropped out of high school and has spent years analysing pictures of the John F. Kennedy assassination, acknowledged he had been paid $8,000 by Simpson's defence team. Asked to describe how important his JFK assassination studies were to him, Groden said, "It's my life's work."
Groden's cross-examination of became so heated that at one point, Simpson attorney Dan Leonard jumped to his feet and complained, "This is character assassination."

Groden, who was called by Simpson's attorneys, testified on Wednesday there was a "high likelihood of forgery" in the 1993 photo, which was taken by a freelance photographer at a pro football game in Buffalo, New York, and later published in the National Enquirer.

The photo, which was introduced earlier by the plaintiffs, shows Simpson wearing the same kind of Italian-made Bruno Magli shoes that left bloody prints near the bodies of Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman. In testimony last month, Simpson denied he ever owned shoes like those in the photo.
